I know I’m not the only one who feels this way. 

I honestly do love social media. The connection to others, the fun, the community.

It’s why when I was studying advertising over a decade ago I started adding in social media campaigns into my pitches.

And then, eventually it’s what I built my whole business on. 

I get to connect with and support so many amazing small business owners. Helping them sell their products and services, reach new people, and build community. 

None of that would be possible without social media. 

But lately it’s felt different. And I know so many other business owners are feeling this way too. 

I want to show up here. I want to help, to inspire, to connect. 

But I also haaaaate how much time I spend looking at screen. How I’m watching other people’s lives instead of living my own. 

Does wanting to delete Instagram and throw my phone into the lake make me a bad social media strategist?? 

I think it actually makes me an even better one. 

I don’t want you spending all your precious time thinking about or creating content. 

I want you living your life!!! Running your business. Doing the things you want to do. 

Not spending hours a day looking for ideas. Feeling like you *~*always*~* need to posting. Doing more.

My whole reason for the Social Goals Club is to help you scroll less and sell more. 

To kick the mental load of social media to the curb so you can focus on more important things in your life!!

Every week I curate four+ trending posts for small businesses in the Club with examples, instructions, and hooks written for you. 

(Plus the library of 100+ ideas to access any time). 

It’s my antidote to the pressure to always be online. Get your content done. Get offline.

MAKE THIS TREND ⤵️

What question or statement would make you back away? Go with that for this “that’s a no from me” reel!

On screen, you’ll add the question or statement (in quotes so people can tell it’s someone else asking or talking). 

Film a continuous video that starts with you standing by your phone, then moving to different spots, each further away from the camera.

In each spot, pause for a moment and give the camera a disgusted, concerned, or confused face.

When editing, delete the space in between your stops using the split tool, doing your best to line it up with audio jumps of the music. 

This is perfect for your showing your unique POV as a business and what you stand for/believe in!!

caption:
Instagram has revealed what’s MOST important for your reel’s performance. 

SKIP RATE 👀

aka what percent of people who watched your reel skipped by it. 

So how do you stop people from skipping by your reels?

🎣 Hook them in with engaging text on screen, visual movement, and clear visuals so they know this content is for them. 

50-60% is average, it’s okay! 
 
30-50% is good, nice work! 
 
Under 30% is excellent, you crushed it! 
 
Skip rates are generally going to be higher in our sales-heavy content which is okayyy! We’re working for sales, not views. 

Not everyone has this update yet but if you do, go investigate your insights on your content to see what reels have the lowest skip rates.

caption:
😮‍💨 One of the biggest reasons why I work on my screen time? 

My kids. 

I don’t want them to think this is what’s normal.

That this is what life is about.

Looking at a phone. Scrolling.

Life is about so much more than this screen. 

That’s why it’s so important for me to help business owners scroll less and sell more. 

Because I want you out there living your life. Not just watching other people live theirs. 

So I am continuously working on what I model to my children.

I will delay my kids’ access to social media as long as possible (thank you @twpiggot for introducing me to @unpluggedcanada - another great resource!).

caption:
Another day, another Instagram change. 🙃

And this time, they’re coming for hashtags.

Right now, some accounts are being limited to just 3 or 5 hashtags per post, instead of the usual 30.

Not everyone has this limit yet (it’s a slow rollout), but this could shape how we use hashtags going into 2026.

👀 What’s Changing

Instagram is testing a hashtag limit of 3–5 per post.

You’ll know you’re affected if you get a pop-up while adding hashtags.

This is a test; not everyone is seeing it yet.

🙏 What’s Staying the Same

Hashtags still help with search and categorization, but they’re no longer the main driver of reach.

Instagram now reads your image, caption, on-screen text, and more to understand your content.

🩷 What To Do Now

Prioritize relevant, not just “related” hashtags.

Use 3–5 specific, strategic tags that reflect your post and what your audience is actually searching for.

Think location-based + niche tags (e.g. PeterboroughFlorist, not just florist).

And most importantly, take a big breath. It’s okay! I’ll be here keeping you updated through all the changes!

Have you seen these limits on your account?

caption:
After over a month of testing, it’s official…

We are now limited to a maximum of 5 hashtags per post. 

Why?

Instagram doesn’t really need hashtags anymore… or at least not in the way it used to. 

Instagram can read your image, caption, on-screen text, and more to understand your content.

So yes, hashtags still help with search and categorization, but they’re not the main driver of reach.

The rest of your content does the heavy work to determine what your post is about and who might be interested in it. 
 
So, what’s a small business owner to do? 

Get specific in your content. 

Weave your location or what you do into your posts.

Instead of “stretches to do this week” it’s “stretches I prescribed my clients this week as a postnatal physiotherapist in Peterborough Ontario” 

Naturally include keywords in your captions and your content.

Add specific hashtags to your posts, relevant to the post. 

Also— You do not need to stack a bunch of keywords at the end of your caption. 

What questions do you have about this change?

MAKE THIS TREND 👇

Jon Hamm is BLOWING UP the internet right now. 

Use this fun + effective trend for extra visibility and connection by sharing a situation your clients and customers can relate to.

0️⃣ Save this trending audio   1️⃣ Click the three dots on bottom right of the screen   2️⃣ Click Remix, then click Open in Edits   3️⃣ In Edits, trim the video to remove my clip

4️⃣ Film yourself in the situation, ending with a happy eyes closed, head slightly turned to the right

5️⃣ Trim your clip as needed to help with the transition from you to Jon Hamm

6️⃣ Add your text on screen for the first clip “When [good thing happens that would result in dancing like Jon Hamm - make it something your clients/customers can relate to]”

7️⃣ Export this clip and save to camera roll

8️⃣ Open a new project in edits and add the video you just saved

9️⃣ Add the trending audio and line it up so the “ooOOhhH” happens right when the switch to Jon Hamm happens

🔟 Share to Instagram

YES, there are more steps than a lot of reel ideas I share but this reel still took me less than 10 minutes to make.

Now it's my job to keep posting about it (does this count? 🤣) so that I remind some of those 1000 people about the service (oh hi).
